_comment: Which chip a model sits under on the shelf, as SETS of general.architecture values.
Hand-curated and dated -- the arch namespace is llama.cpp's and the chips are gatto's, so
no generator can produce this file. What IS mechanical is the check: every arch named here
must exist in llama-architectures.json, and every arch there that carries a family's own
naming stem must be named here or excluded below with a reason. A build fails on either.
The one-directional check is the trap this file was born from. A validator that only asks
'does this arch exist' cannot see an arch that exists and was LEFT OUT -- which is exactly
how six qwen and four gemma architectures went missing from the first draft unnoticed.
R52's discipline, inherited: this file bumps in the SAME COMMIT as llama-architectures.json,
and a test reads both. A set generated from one release and shipped beside another is worse
It answers WHICH CHIP and nothing else. No quality flag, no recommendation, no positive
predicate a caller could render as a tick -- the same asymmetry SupportedArchitectures keeps
by shipping WillNotLoad and deliberately having no Supports.
_ladder_comment: Render order, and it is a decision: gemma first is what the least expert user sees, and
'all' closes the row because it is the way out of a filter rather than another filter.
_families_comment: standalone = a model that gets its own row. variant = a same-origin BUILD of one, folded
into the row it belongs to and never rendered alone.
Two axes, and conflating them deletes a feature: family membership controls what is LISTED,
the cardData.base_model fold controls what gets a ROW. gemma4-assistant is Gemma 4's
speculative-decoding draft model -- the gemma equivalent of qwen's -MTP repos, which the pane
already renders as 'speculative head inside'. Excluding it would never list its repos, so they
would never fold, and EVERY Gemma 4 row would silently lose its builds-zone option.
A variant-arch repo with no base_model is DROPPED rather than rendered: losing a build option
quietly beats offering a draft model as though it were something to talk to.

_arch_tiers_comment: §5.2's other half: 'each arch carries a tier -- dated, hand-reviewed'. D7 narrowed the
QWEN family to a name-parsed tier because there is no qwen36 arch; it did not repeal tiers
for the families where the arch IS the honest key. gemma4 vs gemma3 is an arch split.
The value is the GENERATION as major[.minor], parsed by the same reader as the pin, so a
shelf's ladder and its current-tier test cannot disagree about what a tier means.
Qwen's arches are deliberately ABSENT: that family is name-parsed and an entry here would
glm-dsa is the one JUDGEMENT in this table and it is flagged for review. It carries no
generation in its name; it is GLM-4's sparse-attention arch, so it sits with glm4. The
alternative is leaving it untiered, which makes it 'unversioned' -- the bucket D7 demoted --
and would hide a live GLM arch from the default shelf. Overturn this row, not the scheme.
_excluded_comment: An arch carrying a family's naming stem that is deliberately NOT on that shelf, with the
reason in one word. The list exists so the second direction of the validator has an answer
other than 'add it to a family' -- and so a new arch cannot arrive unclassified.
Every reason here is about LISTING and never about display. 'Exclude it so it stays off the
shelf' is the move that deletes the builds zone: see gemma4-assistant above, which is
excluded from nothing and rendered as nothing.
_current_comment: The DATED PIN for each family whose tier is parsed from the model NAME rather than the arch.
Never derived from a listing: a default shelf that moved the day a publisher uploaded
something would answer a different question every morning.
Only qwen needs one. gemma, deepseek, glm and mistral stay arch-keyed, where gemma4 vs gemma3
IS an arch split and the arch is the honest key. llama.cpp mints no arch per minor bump, so
Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 report the same one and the name is the only thing that can tell them
